head: 804346cf
summary: Substantive surface lands cleanly. All 4 ratified input constraints (R1 no-opaque-arm, R3 ONE-signed-artifact, H+1.1 monotonic-narrowing, H+1.1 decidable contains, NAMED-not-opaque extension slots) are preserved + structurally pinned by the tf3b_* test corpus. Cross-language atomic mirror (Rust+TS+ERROR-CATALOG.md+CATALOG_VARIANT_COUNT 171→173) is correct. Crypto-agility-contract:6 ed25519 routing through benten_crypto_suite::primitives is preserved (no direct ed25519-dalek dep added). CapabilityPolicy sealed-trait discipline (CLAUDE.md baked-in #7) untouched. Both §3.5n ground-truth-verify findings agreed. Two MINOR fixes required: (a) lib.rs:91-94 + 169 doc-drift falsely claiming Scope is #[non_exhaustive] (contradicts scope.rs:33-44 source-of-truth + the no-opaque-arm rationale); (b) chain_validator.rs:25 + 109-111 dead-code _restricted_spec_anchor wrapper. One OBS for the drift-detect workaround follow-up (BELONGS-NAMED-NOW to a new issue).

findings.title: Doc-drift in lib.rs falsely claims Scope is #[non_exhaustive]
findings.evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/lib.rs:89-94 module-doc says "`#[non_exhaustive]` so future named arms are a minor-version bump; any proposal to re-introduce opaque-refinement-witness semantics must be rejected per HARD RULE 12." — but the actual scope.rs:33-44 source-of-truth attribute block + agent's §3.5n finding-1 explicitly DOES NOT apply `#[non_exhaustive]` to Scope (the §1.A.FROZEN item 15(c) freeze is structurally stronger). lib.rs line 156 module-prelude comment is consistent ("v1-frozen `RestrictedSpec` + `Scope`"), but the lines 89-94 block contradicts the actual structural pin. §3.5b pim-1 adjacent-doc-coupling sweep missed this drift.
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW (follow-up commit on same PR; orchestrator-inline if reviewer-cycle is closed: rewrite lib.rs:89-94 to say `"// NOT `#[non_exhaustive]` per the §1.A.FROZEN item 15(c) \"no-opaque-arm\" freeze; future agents proposing a third arm trip compile-error at downstream exhaustive matches rather than wildcard-permitted silent addition. Adding any third arm is a HALT-AND-SURFACE-TO-BEN escalation per HARD RULE 12."`)

findings.title: Dead-code _restricted_spec_anchor in chain_validator.rs
findings.evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/chain_validator.rs:109-111 carries `#[allow(dead_code)] fn _restricted_spec_anchor(_: &RestrictedSpec) {}` with comment "Suppress unused-import warning when this module compiles standalone." — but the `use crate::restricted_spec::RestrictedSpec;` at line 25 IS actually unused at the type level (method dispatch via `parent_spec.contains(child_spec)` does not require the type import; Scope::RestrictedSelector's payload is the type-establishing site). Cleaner fix: delete BOTH the import (line 25) AND the anchor fn (lines 109-111). Net 3 LOC removal; no behaviour change; closes the dead-code surface that violates §3.5b pim-1 adjacent-doc-coupling discipline (the anchor fn's purpose-comment is wrong since stable-clippy passed without it — no unused-import warning would fire).
findings.disposition: FIX-NOW (follow-up commit on same PR; orchestrator-inline trivial: rm import + rm fn body)

findings.title: drift-detect single-line regex workaround — file BELONGS-NAMED-NOW follow-up issue
findings.evidence: crates/benten-errors/src/lib.rs:1409-1417 carries `#[rustfmt::skip]` + comment explaining the drift-detect `buildVariantCodeMap` single-line-regex limitation that wraps long ErrorCode names + bypasses the mapper. Agent's resolution is correct for the wave-scope (G-CORE-3b cannot fix the drift-detect tool — out of scope), but the workaround is per-future-long-ErrorCode-arm-recurrent + the rule is fragile (a fresh agent unaware of the constraint hits the same trap). Per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b) BELONGS-NAMED-NOW: file a follow-up issue NOW naming the drift-detect tool fix as the proper resolution; pim-N candidate per agent's PR-body inline suggestion ("ErrorCode arm names must fit single-line OR carry `#[rustfmt::skip]`" for §3.5g).
findings.disposition: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW (orchestrator to file a new issue: `scripts/drift-detect.ts::buildVariantCodeMap` regex fragility — handle multi-line `ErrorCode::Variant => "E_*"` arms or codify the `#[rustfmt::skip]` per-long-arm convention in §3.5g. Reference back to this finding + the agent's PR body suggestion.)

findings.title: ChainValidatorOutcome enum has a single Admitted arm — Result<(), ChainValidationError> is the more idiomatic shape
findings.evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/chain_validator.rs:28-34 + 70 returns `Result<ChainValidatorOutcome, ChainValidationError>` where `ChainValidatorOutcome` has exactly one arm `Admitted`. The single-arm enum carries no information beyond `Ok(())`. Future #[non_exhaustive] extension is plausible (e.g. `AdmittedWithCaveats`) but the v1-frozen surface should commit to the shape. Suggestion: either (a) reduce return to `Result<(), ChainValidationError>` for terse callsite-ergonomics, OR (b) document the Outcome enum's forward-compat intent explicitly in its doc-comment. Not blocking — pure ergonomic OBS for v1-API-freeze (G-CORE-9) consideration.
findings.disposition: OUT-OF-SCOPE (G-CORE-3b ratifies the public surface as the v1-frozen shape per §1.A.FROZEN item 15(b); the shape is named in the test corpus + can be revisited at G-CORE-9 freeze if the single-arm pattern is judged unnecessary; not a wave-blocker)

findings.title: RestrictedSpec::contains 6-dim composition is O(N*M) per allowlist dimension
findings.evidence: crates/benten-caps/src/restricted_spec.rs:285-294 `allowlist_subset_check` + line 259 label_denylist check use nested `iter().all(|c| iter().any(|p| p == c))` — O(N*M) per dim. For typical Phase-4 plugin manifests where N/M ≤ 8 this is unmeasurable; for adversarial inputs (a chain validator called with attacker-crafted 10K-element allowlists) the chain validator becomes a DoS vector. Mitigation: BTreeSet/HashSet subset check is O((N+M) log N); the public API stays Vec<T>-shaped. v1-assessment-window OBS — name in phase-4-backlog.md if not already.
findings.disposition: BELONGS-NAMED-NOW (orchestrator: add a row to `docs/future/phase-4-backlog.md §3.10 S&C` or successor (v1-assessment-window) naming: `RestrictedSpec::contains O(N*M) allowlist subset → O((N+M)log N) BTreeSet swap; bound max RestrictedSpec dimension size at validator-entry as DoS defense.`)

ground_truth_verify.non_exhaustive_call: agreed — applying `#[non_exhaustive]` to `Scope` would force external-crate matches (which `tests/tf3b_no_opaque_selector_arm_structural.rs` IS, since `tests/` files are external crates not the owning crate) to either use a wildcard arm (silently accepting future `OpaqueSelector` — the EXACT failure mode the test exists to prevent) OR rely on the `non_exhaustive_omitted_patterns` lint which doesn't fire from external crates. NOT applying `#[non_exhaustive]` is the structurally correct choice — the §1.A.FROZEN item 15(c) `no-opaque-arm` freeze IS load-bearing-stronger than the META #907 general default. Agent's resolution is right. (DOC-DRIFT in lib.rs:89-94 is a separate finding r5mr-1.)
ground_truth_verify.drift_detect_workaround: agreed — `#[rustfmt::skip]` + inline-comment is the right wave-scope answer (drift-detect tool fix is genuinely out-of-scope for G-CORE-3b's mint-the-surface mandate). Per HARD RULE 12 clause-(b), file the proper-fix as a BELONGS-NAMED-NOW follow-up issue (captured at finding r5mr-3). The pim-N candidate agent surfaced (`#[rustfmt::skip]` discipline for §3.5g cross-language rule-mirror long-arms) is also reasonable — orchestrator can promote to dispatch-conventions if 3+-instance recurrence.
